gp.heading: Cost of Sales and Gross Profit
gp.text: Cost of sales was $6,056,382 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1,637,228 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $4,419,154, or approximately 269.9%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, cost of sales was $14,803,966, compared to $7,868,710 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $6,935,256, or approximately 88.1%. The increase in cost of sales principally reflects higher brokerage cost of sales, including liquidity-provider, rebate, payment-processing, and clearing costs, which was $4,474,097 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 (compared to $60,237 for the comparable prior-year period) and $10,016,018 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (compared to $3,458,121). Brokerage cost of sales is presented net of intercompany technology and service fees charged by the Company to Crestmark Trading Ltd. of $214,506 and $648,567 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, which have been eliminated in consolidation. Brokerage cost of sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026, exceeded brokerage revenue for the quarter, reflecting rebate and liquidity-provider costs incurred on client trading volumes that were not matched by corresponding trading revenue during the period.

oi.heading: Operating Income
oi.text: Operating loss was $(6,462,702) for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to operating income of $638,620 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $7,101,322. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operating income was $7,780,074, compared to operating income of $879,920 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $6,900,154. The nine-month increase in operating income reflects the increase in gross profit described above, partially offset by the increase in total operating expenses, while the third-quarter operating loss reflects the gross loss for the quarter together with higher general and administrative expenses.

opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text: Total operating expenses were $4,078,095 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3,596,524 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $481,571, or approximately 13.4%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total operating expenses were $13,340,702, compared to $8,520,481 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $4,820,221, or approximately 56.6%. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the increase reflects higher general and administrative expense of $3,955,799 (compared to $3,234,153, an increase of $721,646, or approximately 22.3%), partially offset by lower sales and marketing expense of $102,376 (compared to $317,379, a decrease of $215,003, or approximately 67.7%) and lower depreciation expense of $19,920 (compared to $44,992, a decrease of $25,072, or approximately 55.7%).

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total operating expenses were $13,340,702, compared to $8,520,481 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $4,820,221, or approximately 56.6%. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the increase reflects higher general and administrative expense of $3,955,799 (compared to $3,234,153, an increase of $721,646, or approximately 22.3%), partially offset by lower sales and marketing expense of $102,376 (compared to $317,379, a decrease of $215,003, or approximately 67.7%) and lower depreciation expense of $19,920 (compared to $44,992, a decrease of $25,072, or approximately 55.7%).

ga.text: The increase in general and administrative expense principally reflects additional compliance, audit, legal, and personnel-related expenses to support the Company’s expanded operating footprint following the AIL acquisition, professional fees and other costs incurred in connection with the Company’s contemplated listing of its common stock on a national securities exchange and the related proposed public offering, and, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, $915,000 of stock-based consulting expense relating to 2,500,000 shares of common stock issued to consultants in August 2026 and a $186,975 provision for doubtful accounts. The decrease in sales and marketing expense reflects a shift toward lower-cost digital channels and reduced tradeshow and travel activity, as further described in Note 2.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense), Net
nonop.text: Total other income (expense), net, was net other income of $163,027 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net other income of $96,632 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $66,395. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total other income (expense), net, was net other income of $469,763, compared to net other expense of $(256,002) for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an improvement of $725,765. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, total other income (expense), net, consisted of other interest income (expense) of $64,353 (compared to $(172,107) for the comparable prior-year period), which is net of $19,200 of debt discount amortization on the Vanquish promissory notes, and other income of $98,674 (compared to $268,739 for the comparable prior-year period). For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, it consisted of other interest income (expense) of $269,649 (compared to $(156,638)) and other income (expense) of $200,114 (compared to $(99,364)). The change principally reflects foreign exchange gains and losses on transactions denominated in currencies other than the functional currency of the applicable subsidiary, interest income on operating cash balances, and other miscellaneous items.

wc.heading: Stockholders’ Equity and Working Capital
wc.text:
As of September 30, 2026, total stockholders’ equity attributable to FDCTech, Inc. stockholders was $34,277,475, compared to $22,657,965 as of December 31, 2025, representing an increase of $11,619,510, or approximately 51.3%. Total stockholders’ equity, including noncontrolling interests, was $34,284,980 as of September 30, 2026, compared to $22,691,288 as of December 31, 2025. The components of stockholders’ equity as of September 30, 2026, consisted of Series A preferred stock and common stock at par value of $450 and $12,532, respectively, additional paid-in capital of $22,532,234, accumulated other comprehensive income of $73,872, accumulated surplus of $11,658,387, and noncontrolling interest of $7,505. The subscription receivable of $(8,000,000) and the Series B preferred stock and related additional paid-in capital of $3,344,300 outstanding at December 31, 2025, were eliminated during the third quarter upon the settlement of the subscription receivable and the conversion of the Series B Convertible Preferred Stock, respectively.

The $11,619,510 increase in stockholders’ equity attributable to FDCTech, Inc. stockholders during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily attributable to: (i) net income attributable to FDCTech, Inc. shareholders of $8,256,902 for the period; (ii) the settlement of the $8,000,000 stock subscription receivable due from Mr.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: Total revenue decreased to $3,671,775 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5,872,372 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $2,200,597, or approximately 37.5%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total revenue was $35,924,742, compared to $17,269,111 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $18,655,631, or approximately 108.0%. The nine-month growth was driven primarily by the Margin Brokerage segment, which contributed $27,261,143 of total revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $8,938,912 for the comparable prior-year period, representing an increase of $18,322,231, or approximately 205.0%, reflecting the contribution of Alchemy International Ltd. (“AIL”) following the closing of the AIL acquisition on November 11, 2025 (with the change of control approved by the Seychelles Financial Services Authority on October 29, 2025), together with the continuing operations of the Company’s other regulated brokerage subsidiaries, Crestmark Trading Ltd. (formerly Alchemy Markets Ltd.) (“AML”) in Malta and Alchemy Prime Ltd. (“APL”) in the United Kingdom.

Wealth Management.text: Founded in January 2016 as a back-office technology solution provider, FDCTech has transformed into a comprehensive, end-to-end trading platform offering foreign exchange (FX), contracts for difference (CFDs), equities, bonds, and wealth management services. Our growth trajectory includes the acquisitions of AD Advisory Services Pty Ltd. (2021), Alchemy Markets Ltd. (2022–2023), Alchemy Prime Limited (2023), Alchemy International Ltd. (2025), and Alchemy Markets (Cayman) Ltd. (2026), together with the establishment of Alchemytech Ltd., now T.I.C.G. Integrated Solutions Ltd. (2024), and Xoala Asia (2025), expanding our global footprint across Australia, Malta, the United Kingdom, Cyprus, Seychelles, Mauritius, and the Cayman Islands.

intro.text: FDCTech, Inc. (“FDCTech,” “the Company,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) is a financial technology company incorporated in the State of Delaware, United States of America, specializing in developing and delivering innovative software solutions and business services to the over-the-counter (“OTC”) brokerage and financial services industries. The Company provides a range of proprietary and third-party technology solutions, including its flagship Condor Trading Technology, which supports multi-asset trading, risk management, and pricing for foreign exchange, equities, commodities, and digital assets. The Company is publicly traded on the OTC markets under the ticker symbol OTC: FDCT and is a fully reporting public company subject to the reporting obligations of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Technology & Software revenues represented 14.6% of total revenues in fiscal year 2025 compared to 6.1% in fiscal year 2024.
Wealth management represented 18.4% of total revenues in fiscal year 2025 compared to 24.1% in fiscal year 2024, reflecting the relative growth of the Brokerage and Technology segments.
Brokerage revenues represented 67.0% of total revenues in fiscal year 2025 compared to 69.8% in fiscal year 2024.

As discussed in Note 2 of the financial statements, 3 (three) of the company’s subsidiaries offer trading services and solutions, specializing in OTC and exchange-traded markets in Europe; this accounted for 67% of the total revenue, and it was generated from Commission, Swap, profit from trading, and net floating profit.
The sales, marketing, and advertising expenses represented 3.82 % and 5.44 % of the sales for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, and 2024, respectively.
Commencement of commercial operations will depend on the successful onboarding of merchants and partners and continuing adherence to FSC requirements.
Investors should not rely upon the financial statements as presented in the Company’s previously filed Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 (filed March 3, 2025).

Our primary sources of liquidity are cash generated from operations, proceeds from financing activities, including related party advances and equity issuances, and cash held at our regulated brokerage subsidiaries.

As an emerging growth company, we are permitted to, and do, rely on exemptions from certain disclosure requirements that are applicable to other public companies that are not emerging growth companies, including exemption from compliance with the auditor attestation requirement in the assessment of our internal control over financial reporting pursuant to Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 and reduced disclosure obligations regarding executive compensation in our periodic reports.
The Trading revenue is the Company’s largest source of revenue.
Investors should not rely upon the financial statements as presented in the Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, as originally filed.
